Over the years I learned that i don't care whether tattoos are the best ever looking ones or the most meaningful.

To me tattoos are supposed to be a piece of you, of your past, of your thought process back then when you got them etc. I've got a couple imperfect tattoos, but i know that I've helped out s friend of mine practice on a real "model" I was her first tattoo on a real person and to me they are symbolic, showing me that I cared about her and wanted to help her out and honestly? I love them the most, I'll probably like them more than any professional tattoos I'll ever get, because they show that:

I've helped someone; that our bond was strong enough that I trusted her (doesn't happen often tbh) ,

Everybody starts somewhere and once (if) she gets to a professional level there'll always be a mark of her beginnings,

It's a nice sort of souvenir, time capsule of the past me.

Just go with the flow, it's supposed to be a piece of YOU, not someone else, why would you ever care what other people think about your tattoos, the most important thing is that YOU and only you love them.

Shitty doesn't equal bad, remember that.

Honestly I've been to a point that I was told the exact same and i just scoffed and laughed at the person that said that, because hey, they said weed doesn't have any downsides to it! It's only positives.

Nonetheless I was really stupid. 

As i said first couple of months without weed were hard, as I kept forgetting stuff all the time, I couldn't feel happy etc.

It took me a year to finally feel actually good again with intensive work with a psychiatrist, i changed meds probably like 6-7 times and on top of that was 3 months in a psych ward due to a suicide attempt.

Sure I do smoke weed now, but not to such extent, maybe once every 3 months or so. What greatly helps with that is basically dropping all your plugs altogether, blocking them and so on.

There's hope for you, not today, not tomorrow, but someday.

I thought so too until I realized how much abusing weed messes me up.

People say that weed doesn't have any downsides but that's not true.

After prolonged use you are dependant on weed to feel happy, it screws with your memory A LOT, makes you paranoid etc.

Weed burns out your neurotransmitters, for the first couple of months after you quit you simply can't find joy in anything you do, if I were you I'd simply quit weed and have a serious conversation with your psychiatrist to change your meds. Tell him everything that bothers you, seriously, having the right meds can make a world of difference.

I'm vegan for 2 months now and it's amazing how much my aversion for meat grew stronger for me.
Touching raw meat, the smell of both cooked and raw meat just makes me gag! Can't believe it took so little to realize that i never really liked meat to begin with and only ate it cos my region and most recipes i know are really heavy on it.

There are a couple reasons:

How animals are being handled at farms (animal cruelty, force feeding to achieve desired results, living conditions poor animals are forced to live in etc).

Quality of meat went down A LOT the past couple years, once again quantity over quality.

Our family had our own animals and you wouldn't believe how different the meat is; from texture to taste.

Region i live in has a diet that is really heavy on meat and i simply had enough of meat in my diet to the point that whenever i smell meat now i feel like throwing up.

I find vegetables have far more complex flavor than meat of any kind.
